newsitem.title: FRANCE: Total makes 2nd find on Venezuela field.
newsitem.headline: Total makes 2nd find on Venezuela field.

text.p: French oil major Total said on Monday it had found "significant new reserves" of oil with a second exploratory drilling in the Jusepin field in northeastern Venezuela.

The drilling showed new reserves at depths of more than 5,000 metres. The well is located 7.8 kms from the initial find and reached a geological structure distinct from the first well, the company said in a statement.
Three production tests over several days on different levels yielded a cumulative flow rate of 10,175 barrels per day (bpd). Total holds 55 percent, Amoco 45 percent of the well.

An accelerated development plan has been drawn up for the structure discovered in March, which produced 14,200 bpd during two production tests on the discovery well. As a result the field will come on stream in the first quarter of 1997.
Total is the operator for an association with Amoco for the Jusepin permit under a 20-year contract signed in November 1993 with Lagoven, a subsidiary of PDVSA, the Venezuelan national oil company.
